items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: around 1918, I was taking press roll lessons from Henry Martin.

ctx.x: And, well, he got his inspiration from Bunk. And I got my inspiration from Henry Martin, Black Benny, Red Happy, Baby Dodds. But Baby Dodds used to play in the Orleans during them times. Yeah. Well, after I got old enough I used to go to dances. I, wherever Baby Dodds was playing I was always there. And actually I got a lot from, learned a lot from him. Oh, sure. Yeah. Well, when I, around 1918, I was taking press roll lessons from Henry Martin. Yeah. He was a left-hander like me.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: That's practically where I got my learning from because he was learning me, you know, and he asked me what way I wanted to set up. So I set up left handed.

ctx.x: When you were a kid, did you play on any toy drums or beat on anything?

No, no, no. I didn't beat on it. All I beat it on was the bottom of my mother's old wash tub or upside the fence, yeah. Yeah. So around 1918 I went to work at the Whitney National Bank as a night port. At that time they had Bud Russel, I know you know him. I've heard him. Ed Darcy was working there. Well Ed Darcy's still with him, yeah, but Bud Russel died. Well I was playing piano with a boyfriend of mine named Shedrick Brewster, but we called him nicknamed Baby Brewster, and we used to play house parties on…
What style? Was it something like Baby Dodds or anything particular about his style you could tell us?
